help.heading: Excel format for student import
help.intro: First row = column headers. Order doesn't matter, matching is case-insensitive.
help.groupNote: Students with the same value in the “Group” column form a group. “-” or empty = no group. Priorities are synced to the first student in the group.
help.example:
First name | Last name | Class | Grade | Group | Priority 1 | Priority 2 | Priority 3 | Priority 4 | Priority 5
Anna       | Miller    | 7a    | 7     | 1     | Chess      | Yoga       | Comics     | Theater    | Cooking
Ben        | Smith     | 7b    | 7     | 1     | Chess      | Yoga       | Comics     | Theater    | Cooking
Carla      | Wilson    | 7a    | 7     | -     | Theater    | Yoga       | Comics     | Chess      | Cooking
help.rule1: Grade must be a number between 5 and 13.
help.rule2: Priority values must exactly match a project name from the “Projects” tab (case-insensitive).
help.rule3: Priorities must all be different from each other.
help.rule4: Empty priority cells are OK (≤5 priorities possible). “-”, “–”, or “—” also counts as empty.
help.rule5: A group with only one member is treated as an individual student.
help.rule6: Correct invalid or duplicate wishes before importing. A warning is shown when group wishes are synchronized to the first member.

optimize.title: Optimization
optimize.solveFailed: The distribution could not be calculated. Please try again.

priority.heading: Weight the wishes
priority.headingInfo: Points per priority rank. The solver maximizes the sum of points awarded across all students. Higher = the solver tries harder to get students into this desired project. Default: 10 / 6 / 3 / 2 / 1.
priority.description: A higher value gives a wish more weight. The defaults particularly favor first and second choices.
priority.label: Wish {{n}}
priority.info1: Points a student contributes when they get their 1st choice project. Higher = the solver favors this assignment more strongly.
priority.info2: Points for the 2nd choice. Should be smaller than priority 1, otherwise priorities 1 and 2 are equivalent.
priority.info5: Points for the 5th choice. Should stay ≥ 0, otherwise priority 5 becomes worse than no assignment at all.

unmatched.label: Without a project
unmatched.infoPre: Penalty points when a student is
unmatched.infoPost: (no project assigned). A very high value (default 1000) makes sure the solver places every student as long as a grade-compatible project still has free spots. Only lower this if you deliberately want to leave students unassigned.

overTarget.label: Above target capacity
overTarget.infoPre: Penalty points for every student who fills a project
overTarget.infoPost: (up to the max capacity). Low values (default 2) mean a "soft target" — projects fill up evenly to their target level before any of them go over. Higher = the solver sticks more strictly to the target.

notInTop5.label: Outside wishes
notInTop5.infoPre: Penalty points when a student ends up in a project that
notInTop5.infoStrong: was not among their top 5 choices
notInTop5.infoPost: (only happens when all 5 choices are full). Default 50: much better than unassigned (1000), but clearly worse than any top-5 placement. Higher = the solver would rather leave spots empty than put a student into an unwanted project.

cohesion.heading: Keep groups together
cohesion.label: Group bonus

info.introPre: Bonus points for each additional group member in the
info.introMid: . Higher = the solver gives up more priority points to keep groups together. At
info.introEnd: groups are treated like individual students.
info.defaultPost: : groups stay together through priority 1-2, more likely to split from priority 3 onward.

cohesion.description: A higher bonus favors keeping groups in the same project. At 0, every student is considered individually.
